title: Teachable, and what the class took away
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Who could you learn from today, if you were open to it?

Jose said: I can learn from a fourteen or fifteen year old. It is not just being a mentor, it is also being a mentoree. Be teachable, because otherwise you will not attract people who can teach you. You have to have that aura of being open and ready to learn.

He said that he tells his children he is one percent of a mentor, because he wants them to be hunters of excellence, seeking people who can help with their beliefs, values and strategies. He creates an attitude of positive expectancy.
He said you can learn from absolutely anybody, and when you look at people as resources, people catch on right away. It could be a catalyst for change, if you have that readiness.
Jose said that the first thing he learned not to do is impulsive decisions, and that he suffers from it too. A partner of his has a response: let me think about it, I will tell you tomorrow.

A student said it is a balance: if you get stuck listening to everyone else, that is a problem, and if you go with your convictions and do not listen to anyone, that is a problem again. At least having awareness of both sides helps you decide.

Jose said that he wants convictions to come from an immense positive belief system, where the opinions of others do not affect you. It is okay to feel vulnerable. A student said: vulnerability in itself is a strength.

A student said: the surge leads to collateral damage, but the damage from speed and action is not nearly as bad as the damage and problems from inaction. Another: it is only failure if you did not try.
Another student: when you have had success for too long, you lose the desire to take risks. Another: set deadlines to create urgency, remove what is not necessary, and think unconventionally.
Another: be good to people sometimes means pushing them to grow, not the candy-coated package that society presents.
What is one thing you will do differently on Monday?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write who you could learn from this week, including someone younger.
Write one impulsive decision you could sleep on.
Write where you are vulnerable and what you can do about it.
Write your biggest takeaway from the book as a class.
Write what you will do differently on Monday.

check.q: What did Jose say you must be to attract people who can teach you?
What did a student say is worse than collateral damage from action?
What phrase did Jose give to slow an impulsive decision?
choices: Let me think about it, I will tell you tomorrow

recap: Stay teachable. Sleep on impulsive calls. Act, because inaction costs more.
